newsitem.title: MEXICO: Europe to aid Mexico on agriculture, construction.
newsitem.headline: Europe to aid Mexico on agriculture, construction.

text.p: The European Union and Mexico will begin a pilot program aimed at boosting Mexico's agricultural and construction material exports across the Atlantic, officials said Wednesday.
"The technical assistance project will cost $1.75 million and will be applied in the next 15 months," Eric Galvin, a European Commission delegate in Mexico, told a business forum.
Seafood, agroindustrial products and arts and crafts also will come under the program, Galvin said.
"It can't be opened up to all sectors, but we have identified the problem areas that have impeded the growth of Mexican exports to Europe," Galvin said.
Mexican exports to the European Union grew by 20 percent in 1995 over 1994 to $3.38 billion, an EU report said.
But Mexican imports from the European Union in 1995 were double that figure at $6.72 billion, a drop of 25.7 percent from 1994.
